parts.note: reads like a crooked trader in any business, but the dealer is the one handing out cards at a table and cheating

explanation.definitionFit: A cheat at cards who deals himself winning hands is the classic crooked dealer.

parts.note: the idiom 'run riot' has a twin with the same meaning, so the word wanted is the one that completes 'running ...' for a frenzied crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd losing its head as it runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To run wild in a frenzy is the fixed phrase with this Malay-derived word.

indicators.note: signals that the letters of the words before it might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone toiling on at a grind in a tedious way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging the letters of GRIND ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull steady hum or speech is tedious, so the word means being monotonous.

explanation.surface: The limit of how much one can laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken garden fence is a ditch boundary hidden from view; the same letters spell the sound of laughing out loud.

explanation.surface: Harsh handling for timber that has not been dried.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is pine or fir timber; raw means not yet seasoned.

indicators.note: suggests the four letters of the word else might appear in another order

explanation.surface: Wondering in what other form swimmers might show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging ELSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakelike fish swim, so they are swimmers.

parts.note: to have seen something is to have spotted it

explanation.walkthrough: SPOTTED DICK is a British steamed suet pudding with currants; 'sweet' is the British word for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: This currant pudding is a dessert, which Britons call a sweet.

clue.text: Berlin tourist used to be financially ruined

explanation.surface: A visitor to Berlin used to do something that leaves one broke.
explanation.walkthrough: Visitors to Berlin used to visit the Berlin Wall; the idiom also means going bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankruptcy is described by the idiom about being pushed against a barrier, and Cold War sightseers visited the barrier dividing the city.

clue.text: Keep in mind that Murphy can supply

explanation.surface: Remember what a man called Murphy can provide.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat is a stock Irish name, and Murphy a stock Irish surname, so obtaining something from Pat Murphy is to receive it from him.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning something by heart is the idiom; and an item obtained from someone named Pat is had from him.

parts.note: looks like a comic song or act, but number means something that numbs, and a comical anaesthetic is the one that makes patients giggle

explanation.definitionFit: Nitrous oxide is a dental anaesthetic that numbs and often makes people giggle.

parts.note: liquidate usually means kill, but here it means to make people wet with a liquid, as a toy gun that squirts does

explanation.definitionFit: A child's squirting toy gun is a weapon that soaks people in liquid.

clue.text: Look and sound like a dog

indicators.note: tells the solver the answer is said the same as the word for the dog

parts.note: a peke is a Pekingese, a small dog breed

explanation.surface: Something that both looks and barks like a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick glance is a brief look.

clue.text: Flag with a tale of heroism

parts.note: to flag is to droop or tire, which is to sag

explanation.surface: A banner bearing a heroic story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is a verb meaning to weaken, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse and Icelandic epics recount heroic deeds, and the word now means any long heroic story.

clue.text: Become ill, get nurse round for the final stage

indicators.note: means the word for looking after a patient goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
to ail is to become ill

explanation.surface: Falling sick and getting a nurse to call at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is only a link; 'Become ill' and 'nurse' are verbs, not a patient's story.
explanation.definitionFit: The last part of anything is its rear portion, as with the back of a procession.

clue.text: Plan to have a drink, say

indicators.note: means the word for a drink is spoken, giving a word that sounds identical but is spelt differently

parts.note: a draught is a single swallow of a drink

explanation.surface: Intending to have a drink, as one might put it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough first version of a scheme or document is a preliminary plan.

indicators.note: in a kitchen surface, cooked suggests the letters of the name are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman named Angela has prepared an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals rearranging ANGELAS, the 'S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered pasta baked with sauce and cheese is a classic Italian dish.

clue.text: Sign for a note in Italian money

parts.note: the lira was Italy's currency before the euro
B is a musical note

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B inside LIRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The scales are a zodiac sign, the seventh of twelve astrological constellations.

clue.text: A girl could be made the object of chivalrous attention

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
taken as written
N, north, is a compass point

clue.text: It hinders progress when I'm breaking a record

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A setback just when one is breaking a record.

explanation.definitionFit: An uneven walk from an injury slows a person down.

clue.text: A point about wood for burning

indicators.note: means the first two pieces go round the outside of the tree

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: A sharp stake around timber meant to be burned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and E around FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in flames is ablaze, that is burning.

clue.text: Apart and sure to be different

indicators.note: says the letters of the two words become something different when rearranged

explanation.surface: Separated and certain things will change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be different' signals rearranging AND SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn into separate pieces, in pieces, is the meaning of this old word.

clue.text: First woman to hold a billiard-stick has been displaced

definitions.note: the clue words describe the person, the answer is the person: one who has been displaced

indicators.note: means the first woman's name wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
a cue is the stick used in billiards

explanation.surface: Eve gripping a billiard cue after being moved out.
explanation.walkthrough: The cue goes in after the second letter of Eve's name; the definition describes the person, so read it as 'one who has been displaced'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person moved out of a danger zone, like a wartime child sent to the country, is someone who has been relocated.

clue.text: Full-back comes to sort out warm-up

indicators.note: means the word for full is read in reverse

parts.note: to be fed is to be full

explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns FED into DEF; 'out' rearranges SORT into ROST; 'comes to' joins them. 'Full-back' looks like a football position.
explanation.definitionFit: Thawing frozen food means warming it up.

indicators.note: read as re-serve, to serve again in a new order, which tells the solver to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Taking money out of a Swiss city's reserve fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' is read as re-serve and signals rearranging GENEVAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking revenge is making someone pay for a wrong.

parts.note: a single word covers both a loud peal of thunder and the hand-slapping noise of an audience

explanation.surface: A prop holds something up; one used by an actor is a stage item.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut holds something up; a stage property is an object handled by performers.

indicators.note: means the letters sit within the two clue words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.definitionFit: A gentle jog is an easy run.

parts.note: reads as a flimsy hairband, but light means luminous, a glowing ring round a saint's head

clue.text: Now this will get you nowhere

parts.note: ways sounds like customs or methods of commerce, but means physical paths along which merchants carry goods

level means even or flat
